meta.title: From Temporary Harnesses to Admitted Evidence
meta.description: A source-backed architecture brief connecting Ouroboros loop evolution, Loss Function Design, OMC UltraQA temporary harnesses, and Lev's typed eval spine.

props.title: From Temporary Harnesses to Admitted Evidence
props.subtitle: OOO loop semantics × LFD loss engineering × OMC hostile harnesses × Lev's one-brain eval path
props.meta: Verified against OMC 5319c3d · LFD design 4f362cb · OOO local evidence snapshot 3e382a3 (upstream has advanced) · Lev working tree 2026-07-16

props.content: **The answer:** eval is the shared spine, but the three prior-art systems solve different layers. OOO decides how a loop learns from failure. LFD designs the objective and its anti-cheat instruments. OMC teaches an agent to invent hostile, task-local probes. Lev should support all three without creating a second harness framework: generated probes become an untrusted `Task Eval Instance`, deterministically admitted and frozen, measured by code, decided by `core/eval`, and retained as replayable XDG evidence.

props.title: Current truth
props.content: The architecture is now documented, but the generic generated-harness runtime is not wired end to end. The declared FlowMind validates; it does not yet provide typed admission, immutable artifact binding, generic observer launch, companion measurement, or EvalDecision-required completion. Required evals are therefore not universally blocking today.

props.label: THE SYSTEM MODEL
props.title: Do not collapse authoring, execution, and authority

props.content:
flowchart LR
  O["OOO: choose the next semantic move"] --> A["LLM authors scenarios / fixtures / probes"]
  L["LFD: define target, constraints, anti-cheat, holdout"] --> P["Pack + inline FlowMind policy"]
  M["OMC pattern: generate hostile temporary harness"] --> A
  A --> D["Draft Task Eval Instance"]
  P --> C["Deterministic admission"]
  D --> C
  C --> X["Frozen manifest + bytes + digests in XDG artifacts"]
  X --> R["Exact setup / execute / observe / cleanup"]
  R --> Q["Code companion measurements"]
  Q --> E["core/eval EvalDecision"]
  E --> G{"Lifecycle route"}
  G -->|pass| S["succeed / advance"]
  G -->|fail| F["repair / reject"]
  G -->|error| H["hold / block"]
  E --> O
props.caption: The LLM may propose evidence-producing instruments. Deterministic code decides whether they are admissible and what the resulting evidence means.

props.title: The clean abstraction
props.content: A generated harness is not a new domain object. It is an authoring mode for the existing `Task Eval Instance`: pack references and inline FlowMind compile the policy; the task supplies current claims and optional generated instruments; `core/eval` remains the only promotion-facing verdict emitter.

props.label: PRIOR ART 01 · OOO / OUROBOROS
props.title: The missing mechanism is not another score — it is feeding evaluation back into intent
props.subtitle: Local source snapshot 3e382a3; upstream HEAD was 456a134 when checked, so exact source claims below are pinned to the inspected snapshot.

props.content:
Ouroboros is a spec-first agent loop: Interview produces an immutable Seed, execution produces an artifact, evaluation scores it, and the evolutionary loop changes the next Seed. The important part is **causal use of the evaluation**. From generation two onward, Wonder sees the ontology, prior evaluation summary, output, lineage, and Seed. Reflect turns that critique into a revised intent. A new Seed is generated, its ontology delta is recorded, and only then does execution resume.

That is stronger than merely storing a drift score. Lev's semantic-control design already borrows OOO's weighted drift model — goal, constraint, and ontology preservation — but the durable lesson is the feedback mechanism: an `EvalDecision` must route a typed next action whose input includes the exact failed measurements and prior lineage.

flowchart LR
  S["Immutable Seed"] --> E["Execute"]
  E --> V["Mechanical → Semantic → Consensus eval"]
  V --> W["Wonder: interrogate result + ontology + lineage"]
  W --> R["Reflect: synthesize a new direction"]
  R --> N["Generate new Seed + ontology delta"]
  N --> E
  V --> C{"Converged?"}
  C -->|yes| Z["Terminal result"]
  C -->|no| W
props.caption: OOO's non-deterministic seams are Wonder and Reflect; lineage, budgets, ontology deltas, convergence gates, and phase transitions are deterministic scaffolding.
What OOO contributes beyond a pass/fail eval runner.

props.title: OOO's best failure fixture
props.content: One captured OOO run reported 12 local tests green while terminal acceptance passed only 2 of 4 criteria. That is the exact class Lev must block: local harness success is an observation, not lifecycle authority. Acceptance policy must still discharge through the current generation's EvalDecision.

props.label: PRIOR ART 02 · LOSS FUNCTION DESIGN
props.title: LFD is eval design plus optimizer containment
props.subtitle: The design is richer than a test harness: it builds the target, anti-cheat surface, holdout, instruments, and bounded optimization loop.

props.label: LOSS FUNCTION ANATOMY
props.title: Four pieces must exist before the loop
1 · Target
props.content: A mechanically measurable desired outcome. The spec is the inner loop; the eval distribution is the outer loop.

props.title: 2 · Constraints
props.content: Budgets, capacity caps, allowed surfaces, safety boundaries, and dual-sided metrics that prevent winning by deletion or inflation.

props.title: 3 · Instruments
props.content: Scorers, linters, probes, status checks, dev examples, hidden holdouts, known-good/bad calibration, and artifact capture.

props.title: 4 · Forced entropy
props.content: Holdouts, perturbations, rare cases, adversarial cases, and repeated samples that keep the optimizer from memorizing the visible score surface.

items.title: Inventory existing tests, CI, tools, and surfaces
items.description: Reuse project-native scorers and identify where truth already lives.

items.title: Lock outcome, budgets, acceptance, and allowed surface
items.description: Define what can change and what evidence counts before exposing a score.

items.title: Build target, constraints, instruments, entropy
items.description: Enumerate at least ten cheap paths and add fences.

items.title: Run known-good, known-bad, leak, and deliberate-failure probes
items.description: A scorer that cannot distinguish these is not safe to optimize.

items.title: Propose → verify → threshold/budget → refine
items.description: Patch the loss function when the loop cheats; do not teach the agent a one-off workaround.

items.title: Operator-owned hidden holdout and reviewed source promotion
items.description: A best visible score never promotes itself.

props.content:
harness/
  score.sh        # numeric score; exit code says whether scorer ran
  lint.sh         # hard constraints and cheap-path fences
  probe.sh        # known-good / known-bad / adversarial calibration
  status.sh       # bounded operator-readable state
eval/
  dev/            # visible inputs; blinded answers
  holdout/        # controller-owned; aggregate results only
LOG.md             # cycles, scores, changes, failures, artifacts

props.caption: The approved LFD contract is already close to Lev's desired evaluator component model.

declare it; pin model/prompt/temp; multi-sample mean/median
rows.lev: retain every raw sample and aggregate in code

props.title: Design contract vs shipped reference
props.content: The LFD design is the right prior art; its shipped reference is not final authority. The reference still permits an 0.8 pass-rate threshold, has partial flake/determinism checks, leaves scaffold stubs to fill, relies on an operator for hidden holdout promotion, and does not guarantee restoring the best candidate. Lev should absorb the contract and pressure-test it, not import its runtime authority.

props.label: PRIOR ART 03 · OMC ULTRAQA
props.title: How OMC actually tells agents to build temporary harnesses
props.subtitle: OMC uses a strong prompt protocol for dynamic QA authoring and a much thinner runtime verdict contract.

props.content:
The UltraQA skill instructs the agent to generate temporary tests, scripts, fixtures, or harnesses **only when they materially improve behavioral confidence and no existing E2E covers the behavior**. It says to prefer project-native tools; keep throwaway artifacts in a temp directory or clearly named fixture area; bound every command with timeouts; inspect both exit codes and output semantics; record every artifact and whether it was committed or removed; preserve unrelated user work; and compare dirty-tree state before and after.

The agent must plan a scenario matrix before declaring success. Hostile cases include malformed input, repeated interruption, prompt injection, cancel/resume, stale state, dirty worktrees, hung commands, flaky tests, and misleading success output. It cycles at most five times: baseline, adversarial E2E, diagnose, fix, retest, clean up, report.

flowchart LR
  T["Task"] --> I["$ultraqa task instruction"]
  I --> P["Plan scenario matrix"]
  P --> B["Run baseline"]
  B --> H["Generate hostile temp harness if needed"]
  H --> R["Run with timeout + semantic checks"]
  R --> Q{"All scenarios pass?"}
  Q -->|no| D["Diagnose → fix → retest; max 5"]
  D --> H
  Q -->|yes| C["Cleanup + structured report"]
  C --> V["qa_verdict: clean + summary + evidence locator"]
  V --> G["Autopilot completion gate"]
props.caption: OMC's authoring protocol is detailed. Its machine-facing stage boundary is intentionally shallow.
UltraQA requires these fields per scenario before it can say YES.

rows.purpose: Stable scenario identity and claimed behavior
Prove no task-local debris or side effects remain

props.title: Absolute imports
props.content: A harness under `/tmp` must import the repository through an absolute path; working-directory luck is not evidence.

props.title: Safe file generation
props.content: Use non-interpolating writers for JS/TS bodies. If a heredoc is unavoidable, quote it and verify the generated file before executing.

props.title: State isolation
props.content: Unset `OMX_ROOT` and `OMX_STATE_ROOT` for isolated probes so ambient operator state cannot create a false pass.

props.title: Setup ≠ product failure
props.content: Classify setup and harness defects separately. Repair the probe and rerun before accusing the product.

props.title: What OMC promotes — and what it does not
props.content: OMC's stage adapter writes a shallow `qa_verdict` (`clean`, `skipped`, summary, evidence locator) into Autopilot state. The completion gate checks that `clean:true` came from the UltraQA stage and has a locator. It does **not** reopen the matrix, validate typed scenario payloads, recompute scores, freeze harness bytes, or promote the harness source. A throwaway harness is deleted unless a human intentionally commits it. The promoted object is the verdict pointer, not a reusable harness.

props.title: Why the loop can still fail open
props.content: The proposal and designs say completion requires EvalDecision, but that is not equivalent to a wired runtime gate. Until every declared evaluation requirement resolves to one admitted subject binding and one current `decided/pass` decision — with missing evidence producing `evaluation_error` — a successful agent exit or local test result can still be mistaken for completion.

flowchart TB
  P["Project .lev"] -->|authored| A["pack refs · inline FlowMind · task claims · lifecycle refs"]
  A --> C["compiled policy + admitted manifest"]
  C --> X["XDG data/state/cache/runtime"]
  X --> R["frozen bytes · samples · stdout/stderr · observations · measurements · receipts · EvalDecision"]
  R --> L["execution ledger seal"]
  L -. refs only .-> P
  R --> U["rebuildable trace / dashboard / replay projection"]
props.caption: No split brain: `.lev` is authored state and references; XDG-backed execution-ledger routes hold runtime truth; pages and dashboards are projections.

props.title: The best-agent-framework answer
props.content: Build a system where agents can invent new scientific instruments at task time, but cannot define physics after seeing the result. Let OOO drive semantic evolution, LFD harden the objective, and OMC-style UltraQA generate hostile probes. Admit every instrument under a precompiled policy; freeze its exact bytes and environment; retain every raw sample; let deterministic companions compute measurements; let only `core/eval` decide; make completion impossible without the current decision; and promote recurring instruments into durable packs only through reviewed calibration. That gives Lev adaptive intelligence without sacrificing civilizational-grade replay, provenance, and authority integrity.
